extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining applicability, making, and overcoming rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation/prior art) in patent examination, including required findings, procedural steps, and form paragraph usage. Focused on examiner practice under various statutory paragraphs and changes pre/post AIPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive entity requirement for 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an international application that entered the national stage as to the United States, 35 U.S.C. 102(e) applies only if the inventive entity of the application is different than that of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that, where there are joint inventors, only one inventor need be different for the inventive entities to be different and a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) is applicable even if there are some common inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 35 U.S.C. 102(a) to apply, the reference must have a publication date earlier in time than the effective filing date of the application, and must not be applicant’s own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(b) can be overcome by several means enumerated (A)–(F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: (A) Persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable from the prior art; (B) Amending the claims to patentably distinguish over the prior art; (C) Perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 by amending the specification to reference a prior application or by filing an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 containing a specific reference to a prior application in accordance with 37 CFR 1.78(a); (D) Filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing prior invention if the reference is not a U.S. patent (or application in the case of a provisional rejection) claiming the same patentable invention (but 1.131 is not acceptable when claims of the reference and application are directed to the same invention or obvious variants; then examiner must consider double patenting or interference); (E) Perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) (foreign priority filing date must antedate the reference and be perfected including certified priority document and English translation if necessary and examiner must establish enablement and description under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph); (F) Perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 by amending the specification or filing an application data sheet as in (C). See MPEP § 715 for 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(a) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(a) can be overcome by similar approaches to 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical methods include (A) arguing patentable distinction, (B) amending claims to distinguish, and (C) filing appropriate affidavits/declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.132 showing the reference invention is not by "another"). See MPEP § 715 and § 716.10 for details; where 1.131/1.132 affidavits apply and their limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e) can be overcome by arguing patentable distinction, amending the claims, or filing appropriate affidavits/declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (A) Persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable; (B) Amending the claims to patentably distinguish over the prior art; (C) Filing an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing that the reference invention is not by "another" (see MPEP § 715.01(a), § 715.01(c), and § 716.10), or filing under 37 CFR 1.131 as appropriate. Note: provisional 102(e) rejections and certain situations (e.g., derivation) have special limitations (see form paragraphs and case law such as In re Bartfeld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining 35 U.S.C. 102(a) vs 102(b) for public use/on sale
rubrics_metrics.description: When public use, sale, or knowledge by others is alleged, the examiner must determine whether 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) applies; 'in this country' means the United States only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If activity is by an entity other than inventors or assignee, both 102(a) and 102(b) may be applicable. If evidence points only to knowledge within the year prior to the effective filing date then 102(a) applies; 102(b) applies if activity occurred more than one year prior to the effective filing date. Do not make a 102(a) rejection if there is evidence that applicant made the invention and only disclosed it to others within the year prior to the effective filing date. See MPEP § 2133.03 for case law on 'public use' and 'on sale' bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority to require information (public use/on sale issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: To resolve public use or on sale issues, an applicant may be required to answer specific questions and explain or supplement evidence of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information sought should be restricted to that reasonably necessary under 35 U.S.C. 132 and 37 CFR 1.104(a)(2). Examiner may consider making a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 where reasonably necessary. A 1- or 2-month time period should be set for reply (or the SSP of the Office action if shorter). Failure to reply in a timely fashion will result in abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133). If not enough information to base a rejection, make a requirement for more information using form paragraph 7.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.104 — Requirement for Information, Public Use or Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard form paragraph to require information when an issue of public use or on sale activity has been raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph warns applicant that failure to fully reply will result in abandonment. Examiner notes: (1) information should be limited to reasonably necessary; (2) set one- or two-month reply period unless SSP; (3) if sufficient evidence exists to establish a prima facie case of public use or on sale, use form paragraph 7.16 to make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(b). See MPEP § 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(c) — abandonment of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), abandonment of the 'invention' (distinct from abandonment of an application) results in loss of right to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2134 for case law setting forth criteria for abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c). Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.10 and ¶ 7.17) when making such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) — foreign patenting statutory bar (four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) establishes four conditions which, if all present, establish a statutory bar against granting a patent in this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four conditions: (A) The foreign application must be filed more than 12 months before the effective filing date of the U.S. application; (B) The foreign and U.S. applications must be filed by the same applicant, legal representatives or assigns; (C) The foreign application must have actually issued as a patent or inventor’s certificate before the filing in the United States (need not be published but rights must be enforceable); (D) The same invention must be involved. If such a foreign patent is discovered, make rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(d). See MPEP § 2135.01 for case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should only search for an issued foreign patent as 102(d) prior art if there is a reasonable possibility that such a foreign patent covering the same subject matter has been granted to the same inventive entity before the U.S. effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider average foreign pendency (varies by country). Search can be accomplished on electronic databases by examiner or staff of the Scientific and Technical Information Center (see MPEP § 901.06(a)). The document relied on must be a patent or inventor’s certificate and not merely a published or laid-open application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection for copending U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copending U.S. patent application discloses subject matter that would anticipate claims in another pending U.S. application having a different inventive entity, the examiner should determine whether a provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) at least one common inventor exists between the applications or the applications are commonly assigned and (2) the effective filing dates are different, a provisional rejection of the later filed application should be made because the earlier filed application, if patented or published, would be prior art under 102(e). The provisional rejection is made under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). It can be overcome in the same manner as 102(e) rejections (see MPEP § 706.02(b)), or by abandoning the applications and filing a new application containing the subject matter of both. The provisional rejection cannot be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer in certain circumstances (see In re Bartfeld). Use form paragraphs 7.15.01 or 7.15.04 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.01 — provisional rejection (pre-/non-published applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate form paragraph for provisionally rejecting a claim under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as anticipated by a copending application with a common assignee or at least one common inventor, where the application being examined was filed before 11/29/00 and not voluntarily published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains the provisional rejection is based on presumption of future patenting of the copending application. It outlines possible ways to overcome (37 CFR 1.132 or 1.131 showings) and notes that the rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Examiner notes provide which circumstances require use of different form paragraphs (e.g., 7.21.01) depending on filing/publication dates and ownership of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and copending applications without common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or common inventor and the application was not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), confidential status under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier filed application as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates of the applications are within 6 months of each other (3 months for simple subject matter) then an interference may be proper. If the earliest effective U.S. filing application will not be published under 122(b), it must be allowed to issue once statutory requirements met; after patent publication it may be used as reference in a 102(e) rejection in the still-pending application as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) — applicant not the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) bars issuance of a patent where an applicant did not invent the subject matter being claimed (i.e., applicant derived the invention from another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must presume the applicants are the proper inventors unless there is proof that another made the invention and that applicant derived the invention from the true inventor. See MPEP § 2137 - § 2137.02 for substantive requirements of 102(f) rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) — priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) provides a basis for rejecting where another inventor made the invention in the United States before applicant and had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it; also forms a basis for interference practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining priority under 102(g), consider dates of conception and reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence of one who was first to conceive and last to reduce to practice, from a time prior to conception by the other. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and § 2138 - § 2138.06 for interference procedure and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules for use of form paragraphs (¶7.07–¶7.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.07 through 7.18 (and related sub-paragraphs) provide standardized wording and must be used in making appropriate 35 U.S.C. 102 rejections; particular form paragraphs must be preceded by specified other paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ¶7.07 (statement of statutory basis) must precede many form paragraphs; ¶7.08 (102(a)) must be preceded by ¶7.07; ¶7.09 (102(b)) must be preceded by ¶7.07 and may be preceded by ¶7.08; ¶7.10 (102(c)) must be preceded by ¶7.07; ¶7.12/7.12.01 distinguish pre-/post-11/29/00 AIPA scenarios for 102(e) and have specific examiner notes about applicability (including RCE and national stage considerations); ¶7.13 (102(f)), ¶7.14 (102(g)) also must be preceded by ¶7.07. Use the precise form paragraph required by the factual and filing-date circumstances of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12 vs 7.12.01 — 102(e) pre-AIPA vs post-AIPA usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.12 is for use when the application being examined was filed before November 29, 2000 and was not voluntarily published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); ¶7.12.01 is for use when the application being examined was filed on or after November 29, 2000 or filed before but voluntarily published under 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.12 includes pre-AIPA statutory text and examiner notes limiting its use. ¶7.12.01 sets out the post-AIPA definitions of 102(e) (including published applications and international application publication language) and contains examiner notes clarifying when to use ¶7.12 vs ¶7.12.01 (e.g., RCEs do not change the original filing date; national stage/international application timing). Always precede with ¶7.07 and other appropriate paragraphs as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.15.02 and 7.15.03 — 102(e) rejections with/without common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.15.02 is used to reject under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) when the applied reference has a common assignee or common inventor; ¶7.15.03 is for when the reference has neither a common assignee nor a common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.15.02 notes it may be overcome by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any disclosed-but-unclaimed invention in the reference was derived from the inventor of the application or by appropriate 1.131 showings. ¶7.15.03 requires insertion of either 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation and identification of the prior art. Patent application publications may only be used if ¶7.12.01 preceded these paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.16 — 35 U.S.C. 102(b) public use or on sale rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard rejection paragraph for claiming rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon public use or sale of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.16 must be preceded either by ¶7.07 and ¶7.09 or by ¶7.103. Bracketed text must include full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.17 — 35 U.S.C. 102(c) abandonment rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard rejection paragraph for claiming rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.17 must be preceded either by ¶7.07 and ¶7.10 or by ¶7.103. Bracketed text must include a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment. See MPEP § 2134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.18 — 35 U.S.C. 102(d) foreign patenting rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard rejection paragraph for claiming rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants' prior foreign patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.18 must be preceded by ¶7.07 and may be preceded by one or more of ¶7.08 to ¶7.10. Bracketed text must specify the applicants' foreign patenting facts relied upon.
